root_cause.text: batman-adv's OGM aggregation logic in batadv_iv_ogm_can_aggregate() assumed a forwarded skb selected for aggregation always had enough tailroom, so after runtime toggling of aggregation it could append to an skb allocated with only packet_len bytes and trigger an skb_put overflow.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that "when OGM aggregation state is toggled at runtime, an existing forwarded packet may have been allocated with only packet_len bytes" and that appending "can hit skb_put overflow conditions," while the fix adds `if (skb_tailroom(forw_packet->skb) < packet_len) return false;` before allowing aggregation.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly states that "when OGM aggregation state is toggled at runtime, an existing forwarded packet may have been allocated with only packet_len bytes" and that appending "can hit skb_put overflow conditions," while the fix adds `if (skb_tailroom(forw_packet->skb) < packet_len) return false;` before allowing aggregation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a tailroom capacity check before aggregating OGM packets to prevent appending data to an skb without sufficient space.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added in batadv_iv_ogm_can_aggregate() to compare skb_tailroom(forw_packet->skb) against packet_len and return false when the available tailroom is smaller than the packet length.
intent_record.how: This prevents aggregation from proceeding when the target skb does not have enough writable space at the tail for the new packet, avoiding attempts to append beyond available buffer capacity and thereby preventing invalid memory writes or failed packet construction.

grouping_result.intent: Add a tailroom capacity check before aggregating OGM packets to prevent appending data to an skb without sufficient space.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by adding a tailroom check before OGM aggregation, preventing skb_put overflow when aggregating into an skb that lacks sufficient tailroom.

candidates.rationale: This size check only compares logical aggregated length against max_bytes and omits verifying actual skb tailroom/capacity. That missing guard allowed aggregation to proceed on an skb allocated with only packet_len bytes, leading to overflow when data was later appended.

This was the next/only remaining gate before allowing aggregation, but it limits packet count rather than ensuring destination skb storage is sufficient. The absence of a tailroom check here embodies the vulnerable logic path.

vuln_statements.explanation: This was the size gate controlling whether aggregation could proceed, but it checked only the computed aggregated length against max_bytes and did not verify the actual skb tailroom/capacity of the forwarded skb. As a result, aggregation could be allowed on an skb allocated with only packet_len bytes, enabling a later skb_put overflow.

This was another final admission check before allowing aggregation, but it constrained only the number of aggregated packets. Because no tailroom check existed alongside it, the function could still approve aggregation onto an skb lacking sufficient append space, contributing to the overflow condition.
